title: What a ZIA web log record is and how its fields are named

prose.text: A web log record describes a web transaction. Most fields are named twice, once for NSS and once for the Insights console.

prose.label: What a record is.
prose.text: {{per-transaction}} The unit of one record is not defined {{gap:record-granularity}}.
Values and caveats of individual fields: [[zia.logs.web-field-semantics]]. Fields that need extra enablement: [[zia.logs.field-enablement]]. Rule attribution: [[zia.logs.web-rule-attribution]].

per-transaction.statement: Web log fields describe a transaction: time is the time and date of the transaction, epochtime its epoch time, and recordid a unique record identifier for each log.

quotes: | %s{time} | The time and date of the transaction.
| %d{epochtime} | The epoch time of the transaction
| %d{recordid} | The unique record identifier for each log

two-names.statement: Each web log field is listed under an NSS format specifier and, where one exists, an Insights Logs column name; the same field can carry different names in the two places.

quotes: The following tables display information about the web log fields and example values for those fields. If applicable, the web log fields are mapped to their corresponding columns in Web Insights Logs (Logs > Insights > Web Insights > Logs).
| %d{reqsize} | The request size in bytes | 1300 | Sent Bytes

no-insights-name.statement: Fields without an Insights name have a blank Insights column or are marked specific to NSS, and the time-part fields are marked as derived from Logged Time.

quotes: If applicable, the web log fields are mapped to their corresponding columns in Web Insights Logs (Logs > Insights > Web Insights > Logs).
| %s{tz} | The time zone. This is the same as the time zone you specified when you configured the NSS feed. | GMT |  |
| %d{recordid} | The unique record identifier for each log |  | This field is specific to NSS |
| %s{company} | The name of the company | Zscaler | This field is specific to NSS
| %02d{ss} | Seconds (0–59) | 48 | This field is derived from Logged Time
| %02d{mm} | Minutes (0–59) | 55 | This field is derived from Logged Time
| %02d{hh} | Hours (0–23) | 22 | This field is derived from Logged Time
| %s{mon} | The name of the month | Oct | This field is derived from Logged Time

insights-renames.statement: Some Insights names differ from the NSS meaning: reqsize appears as Sent Bytes, respsize as Received Bytes, and riskscore as Suspicious Content.

quotes: | %d{reqsize} | The request size in bytes | 1300 | Sent Bytes
| %d{respsize} | The total size of the HTTP response, including the header and payload, in bytes | 10500 | Received Bytes
| %d{riskscore} | The Page Risk Index score of the destination URL.
The range is 0–100, from the lowest to the highest risk. | 10 | Suspicious Content

pcap-capture.statement: The pcapid field holds the path of the packet capture file, formatted as company ID, directory and file name, where the directory is the log type; the file is downloaded from the Capture column of Web Insights Logs.

quotes: | %s{pcapid} | The path of the packet capture (PCAP) file that captured the transaction. The PCAP ID has the following format: <Company ID>/<Directory>/<PCAP File Name>.
The directory is the log type. To download the PCAP file, go to the Capture column on the Web Insights Logs page.

psedge-field.statement: The trafficredirectmethod field records the traffic forwarding method used to reach ZIA Public Service Edges.

quotes: | %s{trafficredirectmethod} | The traffic forwarding method to Public Service Edges for Internet & SaaS (ZIA)

record-granularity.title: What exactly one web record covers
record-granularity.detail: Unverified legacy statement: one record is one HTTP or HTTPS transaction observed by a ZIA Public Service Edge. The field CSV describes fields of the transaction but does not define the unit. For HTTPS without inspection the CONNECT and tunneled traffic may be recorded differently. A deliberate test of a plain, an inspected and an uninspected HTTPS request would show it.
